personae.name: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
personae.blurb: Twin brothers and sons to Egeon and ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE, Emilia, but unknown to each other

personae.name: EMILIA
personae.blurb: Wife to Egeon, an Abbess at Ephesus

scenes.setting: A hall in the Duke’s palace

lines.text: Enter Duke, Egeon, Jailer, Officers and other Attendants.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Proceed, Solinus, to procure my fall,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And by the doom of death end woes and all.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Merchant of Syracusa, plead no more.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I am not partial to infringe our laws.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: The enmity and discord which of late

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Sprung from the rancorous outrage of your Duke

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To merchants, our well-dealing countrymen,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Who, wanting guilders to redeem their lives,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Have seal’d his rigorous statutes with their bloods,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Excludes all pity from our threat’ning looks.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For since the mortal and intestine jars

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: ’Twixt thy seditious countrymen and us,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: It hath in solemn synods been decreed,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Both by the Syracusians and ourselves,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To admit no traffic to our adverse towns;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Nay more, if any born at Ephesus

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Be seen at Syracusian marts and fairs;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Again, if any Syracusian born

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Come to the bay of Ephesus, he dies,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: His goods confiscate to the Duke’s dispose,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Unless a thousand marks be levied

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To quit the penalty and to ransom him.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Thy substance, valued at the highest rate,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Cannot amount unto a hundred marks;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Therefore by law thou art condemn’d to die.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Yet this my comfort; when your words are done,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: My woes end likewise with the evening sun.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Well, Syracusian, say in brief the cause

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Why thou departedst from thy native home,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And for what cause thou cam’st to Ephesus.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: A heavier task could not have been impos’d

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Than I to speak my griefs unspeakable;

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Yet, that the world may witness that my end

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Was wrought by nature, not by vile offence,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: I’ll utter what my sorrow gives me leave.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: In Syracusa was I born, and wed

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Unto a woman happy but for me,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And by me, had not our hap been bad.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: With her I liv’d in joy; our wealth increas’d

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: By prosperous voyages I often made

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: To Epidamnum, till my factor’s death,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And the great care of goods at random left,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Drew me from kind embracements of my spouse;

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: From whom my absence was not six months old

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Before herself (almost at fainting under

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: The pleasing punishment that women bear)

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Had made provision for her following me,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And soon and safe arrived where I was.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: There had she not been long but she became

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: A joyful mother of two goodly sons,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And, which was strange, the one so like the other

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: As could not be distinguish’d but by names.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: That very hour, and in the self-same inn,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: A mean woman was delivered

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Of such a burden, male twins, both alike.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Those, for their parents were exceeding poor,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: I bought, and brought up to attend my sons.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: My wife, not meanly proud of two such boys,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Made daily motions for our home return.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Unwilling I agreed; alas, too soon

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: We came aboard.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: A league from Epidamnum had we sail’d

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Before the always-wind-obeying deep

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Gave any tragic instance of our harm;

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: But longer did we not retain much hope;

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: For what obscured light the heavens did grant

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Did but convey unto our fearful minds

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: A doubtful warrant of immediate death,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Which though myself would gladly have embrac’d,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Yet the incessant weepings of my wife,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Weeping before for what she saw must come,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And piteous plainings of the pretty babes,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: That mourn’d for fashion, ignorant what to fear,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Forc’d me to seek delays for them and me.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And this it was (for other means was none).

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: The sailors sought for safety by our boat,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And left the ship, then sinking-ripe, to us.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: My wife, more careful for the latter-born,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Had fast’ned him unto a small spare mast,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Such as sea-faring men provide for storms.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: To him one of the other twins was bound,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Whilst I had been like heedful of the other.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: The children thus dispos’d, my wife and I,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Fixing our eyes on whom our care was fix’d,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Fast’ned ourselves at either end the mast,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And, floating straight, obedient to the stream,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Was carried towards Corinth, as we thought.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: At length the sun, gazing upon the earth,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Dispers’d those vapours that offended us,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And by the benefit of his wished light

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: The seas wax’d calm, and we discovered

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Two ships from far, making amain to us,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Of Corinth that, of Epidaurus this.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: But ere they came—O, let me say no more!

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Gather the sequel by that went before.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Nay, forward, old man, do not break off so,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: For we may pity, though not pardon thee.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: O, had the gods done so, I had not now

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Worthily term’d them merciless to us.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: For, ere the ships could meet by twice five leagues,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: We were encountered by a mighty rock,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Which being violently borne upon,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Our helpful ship was splitted in the midst;

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: So that, in this unjust divorce of us,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Fortune had left to both of us alike

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: What to delight in, what to sorrow for.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Her part, poor soul, seeming as burdened

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: With lesser weight, but not with lesser woe,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Was carried with more speed before the wind,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And in our sight they three were taken up

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: By fishermen of Corinth, as we thought.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: At length another ship had seiz’d on us;

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And, knowing whom it was their hap to save,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Gave healthful welcome to their ship-wrack’d guests,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And would have reft the fishers of their prey,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Had not their bark been very slow of sail;

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And therefore homeward did they bend their course.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Thus have you heard me sever’d from my bliss,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: That by misfortunes was my life prolong’d

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: To tell sad stories of my own mishaps.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And for the sake of them thou sorrowest for,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Do me the favour to dilate at full

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: What have befall’n of them and thee till now.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: My youngest boy, and yet my eldest care,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: At eighteen years became inquisitive

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: After his brother, and importun’d me

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: That his attendant, so his case was like,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Reft of his brother, but retain’d his name,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Might bear him company in the quest of him;

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Whom whilst I laboured of a love to see,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: I hazarded the loss of whom I lov’d.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Five summers have I spent in farthest Greece,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Roaming clean through the bounds of Asia,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And, coasting homeward, came to Ephesus,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Hopeless to find, yet loath to leave unsought

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Or that or any place that harbours men.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: But here must end the story of my life;

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And happy were I in my timely death,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Could all my travels warrant me they live.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Hapless Egeon, whom the fates have mark’d

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To bear the extremity of dire mishap;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Now, trust me, were it not against our laws,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Against my crown, my oath, my dignity,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Which princes, would they, may not disannul,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: My soul should sue as advocate for thee.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But though thou art adjudged to the death,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And passed sentence may not be recall’d

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But to our honour’s great disparagement,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Yet will I favour thee in what I can.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Therefore, merchant, I’ll limit thee this day

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: To seek thy health by beneficial help.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Try all the friends thou hast in Ephesus;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Beg thou, or borrow, to make up the sum,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And live; if no, then thou art doom’d to die.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Jailer, take him to thy custody.

lines.speaker: JAILER
lines.text: I will, my lord.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Hopeless and helpless doth Egeon wend,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: But to procrastinate his lifeless end.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Antipholus and Dromio of Syracuse and a Merchant.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Therefore give out you are of Epidamnum,

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Lest that your goods too soon be confiscate.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: This very day a Syracusian merchant

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Is apprehended for arrival here,

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: And, not being able to buy out his life,

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: According to the statute of the town

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Dies ere the weary sun set in the west.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: There is your money that I had to keep.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Go bear it to the Centaur, where we host,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And stay there, Dromio, till I come to thee.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Within this hour it will be dinnertime;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Till that, I’ll view the manners of the town,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Peruse the traders, gaze upon the buildings,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And then return and sleep within mine inn,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: For with long travel I am stiff and weary.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Get thee away.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Many a man would take you at your word,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And go indeed, having so good a mean.
[_Exit Dromio._]

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: A trusty villain, sir, that very oft,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: When I am dull with care and melancholy,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Lightens my humour with his merry jests.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What, will you walk with me about the town,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And then go to my inn and dine with me?

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: I am invited, sir, to certain merchants,

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Of whom I hope to make much benefit.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: I crave your pardon. Soon, at five o’clock,

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Please you, I’ll meet with you upon the mart,

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: And afterward consort you till bedtime.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: My present business calls me from you now.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Farewell till then: I will go lose myself,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And wander up and down to view the city.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Sir, I commend you to your own content.
[_Exit Merchant._]

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: He that commends me to mine own content

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Commends me to the thing I cannot get.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I to the world am like a drop of water

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: That in the ocean seeks another drop,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Who, failing there to find his fellow forth,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Unseen, inquisitive, confounds himself.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: So I, to find a mother and a brother,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: In quest of them, unhappy, lose myself.
Enter Dromio of Ephesus.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Here comes the almanac of my true date.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What now? How chance thou art return’d so soon?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Return’d so soon? rather approach’d too late.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: The capon burns, the pig falls from the spit;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: The clock hath strucken twelve upon the bell;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: My mistress made it one upon my cheek.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: She is so hot because the meat is cold;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: The meat is cold because you come not home;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: You come not home because you have no stomach;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: You have no stomach, having broke your fast;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But we that know what ’tis to fast and pray,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Are penitent for your default today.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Stop in your wind, sir, tell me this, I pray:

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Where have you left the money that I gave you?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: O, sixpence that I had o’ Wednesday last

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: To pay the saddler for my mistress’ crupper:

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: The saddler had it, sir, I kept it not.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I am not in a sportive humour now.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Tell me, and dally not, where is the money?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: We being strangers here, how dar’st thou trust

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: So great a charge from thine own custody?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I pray you jest, sir, as you sit at dinner:

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I from my mistress come to you in post;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: If I return, I shall be post indeed,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: For she will score your fault upon my pate.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Methinks your maw, like mine, should be your clock,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And strike you home without a messenger.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Come, Dromio, come, these jests are out of season,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Reserve them till a merrier hour than this.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Where is the gold I gave in charge to thee?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: To me, sir? why, you gave no gold to me!

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Come on, sir knave, have done your foolishness,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And tell me how thou hast dispos’d thy charge.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: My charge was but to fetch you from the mart

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Home to your house, the Phoenix, sir, to dinner.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: My mistress and her sister stay for you.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Now, as I am a Christian, answer me

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: In what safe place you have bestow’d my money,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Or I shall break that merry sconce of yours

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: That stands on tricks when I am undispos’d;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Where is the thousand marks thou hadst of me?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I have some marks of yours upon my pate,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Some of my mistress’ marks upon my shoulders,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But not a thousand marks between you both.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: If I should pay your worship those again,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Perchance you will not bear them patiently.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Thy mistress’ marks? what mistress, slave, hast thou?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Your worship’s wife, my mistress at the Phoenix;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: She that doth fast till you come home to dinner,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And prays that you will hie you home to dinner.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What, wilt thou flout me thus unto my face,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Being forbid? There, take you that, sir knave.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: What mean you, sir? for God’s sake hold your hands.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Nay, an you will not, sir, I’ll take my heels.
[_Exit Dromio._]

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Upon my life, by some device or other

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: The villain is o’er-raught of all my money.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: They say this town is full of cozenage,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: As nimble jugglers that deceive the eye,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Dark-working sorcerers that change the mind,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Soul-killing witches that deform the body,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Disguised cheaters, prating mountebanks,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And many such-like liberties of sin:

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: If it prove so, I will be gone the sooner.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I’ll to the Centaur to go seek this slave.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I greatly fear my money is not safe.
[_Exit._]
Enter Adriana, wife to Antipholus (of Ephesus) with Luciana her sister.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Neither my husband nor the slave return’d

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: That in such haste I sent to seek his master?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Sure, Luciana, it is two o’clock.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Perhaps some merchant hath invited him,

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: And from the mart he’s somewhere gone to dinner.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Good sister, let us dine, and never fret;

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: A man is master of his liberty;

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Time is their master, and when they see time,

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: They’ll go or come. If so, be patient, sister.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Why should their liberty than ours be more?

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Because their business still lies out o’ door.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Look when I serve him so, he takes it ill.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: O, know he is the bridle of your will.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: There’s none but asses will be bridled so.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Why, headstrong liberty is lash’d with woe.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: There’s nothing situate under heaven’s eye

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: But hath his bound in earth, in sea, in sky.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: The beasts, the fishes, and the winged fowls

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Are their males’ subjects, and at their controls.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Man, more divine, the masters of all these,

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Lord of the wide world and wild wat’ry seas,

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Indued with intellectual sense and souls,

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Of more pre-eminence than fish and fowls,

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Are masters to their females, and their lords:

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Then let your will attend on their accords.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: This servitude makes you to keep unwed.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Not this, but troubles of the marriage-bed.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: But, were you wedded, you would bear some sway.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Ere I learn love, I’ll practise to obey.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: How if your husband start some other where?

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Till he come home again, I would forbear.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Patience unmov’d! No marvel though she pause;

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: They can be meek that have no other cause.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: A wretched soul bruis’d with adversity,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: We bid be quiet when we hear it cry;

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: But were we burd’ned with like weight of pain,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: As much, or more, we should ourselves complain:

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: So thou, that hast no unkind mate to grieve thee,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: With urging helpless patience would relieve me:

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: But if thou live to see like right bereft,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: This fool-begg’d patience in thee will be left.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Well, I will marry one day, but to try.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Here comes your man, now is your husband nigh.
Enter Dromio of Ephesus.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Say, is your tardy master now at hand?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Nay, he’s at two hands with me, and that my two ears can witness.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Say, didst thou speak with him? know’st thou his mind?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Ay, ay, he told his mind upon mine ear.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Beshrew his hand, I scarce could understand it.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Spake he so doubtfully thou couldst not feel his meaning?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Nay, he struck so plainly I could too well feel his blows; and withal

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: so doubtfully that I could scarce understand them.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: But say, I prithee, is he coming home?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: It seems he hath great care to please his wife.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Why, mistress, sure my master is horn-mad.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Horn-mad, thou villain?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I mean not cuckold-mad,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But sure he’s stark mad.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: When I desir’d him to come home to dinner,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: He ask’d me for a thousand marks in gold.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: “’Tis dinner time,” quoth I. “My gold,” quoth he.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: “Your meat doth burn” quoth I. “My gold,” quoth he.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: “Will you come home?” quoth I. “My gold,” quoth he.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: “Where is the thousand marks I gave thee, villain?”

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: “The pig” quoth I “is burn’d”. “My gold,” quoth he.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: “My mistress, sir,” quoth I. “Hang up thy mistress;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I know not thy mistress; out on thy mistress!”

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Quoth who?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Quoth my master.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: “I know,” quoth he, “no house, no wife, no mistress.”

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: So that my errand, due unto my tongue,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I thank him, I bare home upon my shoulders;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: For, in conclusion, he did beat me there.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Go back again, thou slave, and fetch him home.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Go back again, and be new beaten home?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: For God’s sake, send some other messenger.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Back slave, or I will break thy pate across.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And he will bless that cross with other beating.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Between you I shall have a holy head.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Hence, prating peasant. Fetch thy master home.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Am I so round with you, as you with me,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: That like a football you do spurn me thus?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: You spurn me hence, and he will spurn me hither.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: If I last in this service, you must case me in leather.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Fie, how impatience loureth in your face.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: His company must do his minions grace,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Whilst I at home starve for a merry look.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Hath homely age th’ alluring beauty took

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: From my poor cheek? then he hath wasted it.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Are my discourses dull? barren my wit?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: If voluble and sharp discourse be marr’d,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Unkindness blunts it more than marble hard.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Do their gay vestments his affections bait?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: That’s not my fault; he’s master of my state.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: What ruins are in me that can be found

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: By him not ruin’d? Then is he the ground

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Of my defeatures. My decayed fair

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: A sunny look of his would soon repair;

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: But, too unruly deer, he breaks the pale

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And feeds from home; poor I am but his stale.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Self-harming jealousy! fie, beat it hence.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Unfeeling fools can with such wrongs dispense.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: I know his eye doth homage otherwhere,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Or else what lets it but he would be here?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Sister, you know he promis’d me a chain;

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Would that alone, a love he would detain,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: So he would keep fair quarter with his bed.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: I see the jewel best enamelled

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Will lose his beauty; yet the gold bides still

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: That others touch, yet often touching will

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Wear gold; and no man that hath a name

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: By falsehood and corruption doth it shame.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Since that my beauty cannot please his eye,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: I’ll weep what’s left away, and weeping die.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: How many fond fools serve mad jealousy!
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Antipholus of Syracuse.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: The gold I gave to Dromio is laid up

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Safe at the Centaur, and the heedful slave

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Is wander’d forth in care to seek me out.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: By computation and mine host’s report.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I could not speak with Dromio since at first

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I sent him from the mart. See, here he comes.
Enter Dromio of Syracuse.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: How now, sir! is your merry humour alter’d?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: As you love strokes, so jest with me again.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: You know no Centaur? you receiv’d no gold?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Your mistress sent to have me home to dinner?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: My house was at the Phoenix? Wast thou mad,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: That thus so madly thou didst answer me?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What answer, sir? when spake I such a word?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Even now, even here, not half an hour since.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I did not see you since you sent me hence,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Home to the Centaur with the gold you gave me.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Villain, thou didst deny the gold’s receipt,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And told’st me of a mistress and a dinner,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: For which I hope thou felt’st I was displeas’d.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I am glad to see you in this merry vein.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What means this jest, I pray you, master, tell me?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Yea, dost thou jeer and flout me in the teeth?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Think’st thou I jest? Hold, take thou that, and that.
[_Beats Dromio._]

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Hold, sir, for God’s sake, now your jest is earnest.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Upon what bargain do you give it me?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Because that I familiarly sometimes

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Do use you for my fool, and chat with you,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Your sauciness will jest upon my love,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And make a common of my serious hours.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: When the sun shines let foolish gnats make sport,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: But creep in crannies when he hides his beams.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: If you will jest with me, know my aspect,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And fashion your demeanour to my looks,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Or I will beat this method in your sconce.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Sconce, call you it? so you would leave battering, I had rather have it

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: a head. And you use these blows long, I must get a sconce for my head,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: and ensconce it too, or else I shall seek my wit in my shoulders. But I

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: pray, sir, why am I beaten?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Dost thou not know?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Nothing, sir, but that I am beaten.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Shall I tell you why?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Ay, sir, and wherefore; for they say, every why hath a wherefore.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Why, first, for flouting me; and then wherefore,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: For urging it the second time to me.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Was there ever any man thus beaten out of season,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: When in the why and the wherefore is neither rhyme nor reason?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Well, sir, I thank you.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Thank me, sir, for what?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Marry, sir, for this something that you gave me for nothing.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I’ll make you amends next, to give you nothing for something.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: But say, sir, is it dinner-time?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: No, sir; I think the meat wants that I have.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: In good time, sir, what’s that?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Basting.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Well, sir, then ’twill be dry.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: If it be, sir, I pray you eat none of it.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Your reason?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Lest it make you choleric, and purchase me another dry basting.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Well, sir, learn to jest in good time.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: There’s a time for all things.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I durst have denied that before you were so choleric.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: By what rule, sir?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Marry, sir, by a rule as plain as the plain bald pate of Father Time

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: himself.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Let’s hear it.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: There’s no time for a man to recover his hair that grows bald by

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: nature.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: May he not do it by fine and recovery?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Yes, to pay a fine for a periwig, and recover the lost hair of another

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: man.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Why is Time such a niggard of hair, being, as it is, so plentiful an

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: excrement?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Because it is a blessing that he bestows on beasts, and what he hath

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: scanted men in hair he hath given them in wit.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Why, but there’s many a man hath more hair than wit.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Not a man of those but he hath the wit to lose his hair.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Why, thou didst conclude hairy men plain dealers without wit.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: The plainer dealer, the sooner lost. Yet he loseth it in a kind of

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: jollity.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: For what reason?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: For two, and sound ones too.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Nay, not sound, I pray you.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Sure ones, then.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Nay, not sure, in a thing falsing.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Certain ones, then.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Name them.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: The one, to save the money that he spends in tiring; the other, that at

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: dinner they should not drop in his porridge.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: You would all this time have proved there is no time for all things.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Marry, and did, sir; namely, e’en no time to recover hair lost by

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: nature.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: But your reason was not substantial why there is no time to recover.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Thus I mend it: Time himself is bald, and therefore, to the world’s end

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: will have bald followers.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I knew ’twould be a bald conclusion.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: But soft! who wafts us yonder?
Enter Adriana and Luciana.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Ay, ay, Antipholus, look strange and frown,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Some other mistress hath thy sweet aspects.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: I am not Adriana, nor thy wife.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: The time was once when thou unurg’d wouldst vow

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: That never words were music to thine ear,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: That never object pleasing in thine eye,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: That never touch well welcome to thy hand,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: That never meat sweet-savour’d in thy taste,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Unless I spake, or look’d, or touch’d, or carv’d to thee.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: How comes it now, my husband, O, how comes it,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: That thou art then estranged from thyself?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Thyself I call it, being strange to me,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: That, undividable, incorporate,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Am better than thy dear self’s better part.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Ah, do not tear away thyself from me;

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: For know, my love, as easy mayst thou fall

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: A drop of water in the breaking gulf,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And take unmingled thence that drop again

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Without addition or diminishing,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: As take from me thyself, and not me too.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: How dearly would it touch thee to the quick,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Should’st thou but hear I were licentious?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And that this body, consecrate to thee,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: By ruffian lust should be contaminate?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Wouldst thou not spit at me, and spurn at me,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And hurl the name of husband in my face,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And tear the stain’d skin off my harlot brow,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And from my false hand cut the wedding-ring,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And break it with a deep-divorcing vow?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: I know thou canst; and therefore, see thou do it.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: I am possess’d with an adulterate blot;

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: My blood is mingled with the crime of lust;

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: For if we two be one, and thou play false,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: I do digest the poison of thy flesh,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Being strumpeted by thy contagion.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Keep then fair league and truce with thy true bed,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: I live distain’d, thou undishonoured.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Plead you to me, fair dame? I know you not.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: In Ephesus I am but two hours old,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: As strange unto your town as to your talk,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Who, every word by all my wit being scann’d,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Wants wit in all one word to understand.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Fie, brother, how the world is chang’d with you.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: When were you wont to use my sister thus?

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: She sent for you by Dromio home to dinner.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: By Dromio?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: By me?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: By thee; and this thou didst return from him,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: That he did buffet thee, and in his blows

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Denied my house for his, me for his wife.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Did you converse, sir, with this gentlewoman?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What is the course and drift of your compact?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I, sir? I never saw her till this time.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Villain, thou liest, for even her very words

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Didst thou deliver to me on the mart.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I never spake with her in all my life.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: How can she thus, then, call us by our names?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Unless it be by inspiration.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: How ill agrees it with your gravity

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: To counterfeit thus grossly with your slave,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Abetting him to thwart me in my mood;

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Be it my wrong, you are from me exempt,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: But wrong not that wrong with a more contempt.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Come, I will fasten on this sleeve of thine.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Thou art an elm, my husband, I a vine,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Whose weakness, married to thy stronger state,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Makes me with thy strength to communicate:

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: If aught possess thee from me, it is dross,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Usurping ivy, brier, or idle moss,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Who all, for want of pruning, with intrusion

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Infect thy sap, and live on thy confusion.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: To me she speaks; she moves me for her theme.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What, was I married to her in my dream?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Or sleep I now, and think I hear all this?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What error drives our eyes and ears amiss?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Until I know this sure uncertainty

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I’ll entertain the offer’d fallacy.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Dromio, go bid the servants spread for dinner.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: O, for my beads! I cross me for a sinner.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: This is the fairy land; O spite of spites!

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: We talk with goblins, owls, and sprites;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: If we obey them not, this will ensue:

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: They’ll suck our breath, or pinch us black and blue.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Why prat’st thou to thyself, and answer’st not?

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Dromio, thou drone, thou snail, thou slug, thou sot.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I am transformed, master, am I not?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I think thou art in mind, and so am I.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Nay, master, both in mind and in my shape.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Thou hast thine own form.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: No, I am an ape.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: If thou art chang’d to aught, ’tis to an ass.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: ’Tis true; she rides me, and I long for grass.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: ’Tis so, I am an ass; else it could never be

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: But I should know her as well as she knows me.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Come, come, no longer will I be a fool,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: To put the finger in the eye and weep

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Whilst man and master laughs my woes to scorn.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Come, sir, to dinner; Dromio, keep the gate.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Husband, I’ll dine above with you today,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And shrive you of a thousand idle pranks.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Sirrah, if any ask you for your master,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Say he dines forth, and let no creature enter.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Come, sister; Dromio, play the porter well.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Am I in earth, in heaven, or in hell?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Sleeping or waking, mad, or well-advis’d?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Known unto these, and to myself disguis’d!

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I’ll say as they say, and persever so,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And in this mist at all adventures go.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Master, shall I be porter at the gate?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Ay; and let none enter, lest I break your pate.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Come, come, Antipholus, we dine too late.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Antipholus of Ephesus, his man Dromio of Ephesus, Angelo the goldsmith and Balthasar the merchant.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Good Signior Angelo, you must excuse us all,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: My wife is shrewish when I keep not hours.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Say that I linger’d with you at your shop

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: To see the making of her carcanet,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And that tomorrow you will bring it home.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But here’s a villain that would face me down.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: He met me on the mart, and that I beat him,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And charg’d him with a thousand marks in gold,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And that I did deny my wife and house.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Thou drunkard, thou, what didst thou mean by this?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Say what you will, sir, but I know what I know.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: That you beat me at the mart I have your hand to show;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: If the skin were parchment, and the blows you gave were ink,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Your own handwriting would tell you what I think.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I think thou art an ass.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Marry, so it doth appear

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: By the wrongs I suffer and the blows I bear.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I should kick, being kick’d; and being at that pass,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: You would keep from my heels, and beware of an ass.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: You’re sad, Signior Balthasar; pray God our cheer

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: May answer my good will and your good welcome here.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: I hold your dainties cheap, sir, and your welcome dear.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: O, Signior Balthasar, either at flesh or fish

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: A table full of welcome makes scarce one dainty dish.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Good meat, sir, is common; that every churl affords.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And welcome more common, for that’s nothing but words.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Small cheer and great welcome makes a merry feast.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Ay, to a niggardly host and more sparing guest.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But though my cates be mean, take them in good part;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Better cheer may you have, but not with better heart.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But soft; my door is lock’d. Go bid them let us in.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Maud, Bridget, Marian, Cicely, Gillian, Ginn!
[_Within._]

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Mome, malt-horse, capon, coxcomb, idiot, patch!

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Either get thee from the door or sit down at the hatch:

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Dost thou conjure for wenches, that thou call’st for such store

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: When one is one too many? Go, get thee from the door.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: What patch is made our porter? My master stays in the street.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Let him walk from whence he came, lest he catch cold on’s feet.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Who talks within there? Ho, open the door.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Right, sir, I’ll tell you when an you’ll tell me wherefore.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Wherefore? For my dinner. I have not dined today.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Nor today here you must not; come again when you may.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: What art thou that keep’st me out from the house I owe?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: The porter for this time, sir, and my name is Dromio.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: O villain, thou hast stolen both mine office and my name;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: The one ne’er got me credit, the other mickle blame.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: If thou hadst been Dromio today in my place,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Thou wouldst have chang’d thy face for a name, or thy name for an ass.
Enter Luce concealed from Antipholus of Ephesus and his companions.
[_Within._]

lines.speaker: LUCE
lines.text: What a coil is there, Dromio, who are those at the gate?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Let my master in, Luce.

lines.speaker: LUCE
lines.text: Faith, no, he comes too late,

lines.speaker: LUCE
lines.text: And so tell your master.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: O Lord, I must laugh;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Have at you with a proverb:—Shall I set in my staff?

lines.speaker: LUCE
lines.text: Have at you with another: that’s—When? can you tell?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: If thy name be called Luce,—Luce, thou hast answer’d him well.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Do you hear, you minion? you’ll let us in, I hope?

lines.speaker: LUCE
lines.text: I thought to have ask’d you.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And you said no.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: So, come, help. Well struck, there was blow for blow.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Thou baggage, let me in.

lines.speaker: LUCE
lines.text: Can you tell for whose sake?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Master, knock the door hard.

lines.speaker: LUCE
lines.text: Let him knock till it ache.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: You’ll cry for this, minion, if I beat the door down.

lines.speaker: LUCE
lines.text: What needs all that, and a pair of stocks in the town?
Enter Adriana concealed from Antipholus of Ephesus and his companions.
[_Within._]

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Who is that at the door that keeps all this noise?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: By my troth, your town is troubled with unruly boys.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Are you there, wife? you might have come before.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Your wife, sir knave? go, get you from the door.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: If you went in pain, master, this knave would go sore.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Here is neither cheer, sir, nor welcome. We would fain have either.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: In debating which was best, we shall part with neither.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: They stand at the door, master; bid them welcome hither.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: There is something in the wind, that we cannot get in.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: You would say so, master, if your garments were thin.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Your cake here is warm within; you stand here in the cold.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: It would make a man mad as a buck to be so bought and sold.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Go, fetch me something, I’ll break ope the gate.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Break any breaking here, and I’ll break your knave’s pate.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: A man may break a word with you, sir, and words are but wind;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Ay, and break it in your face, so he break it not behind.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: It seems thou want’st breaking; out upon thee, hind!

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Here’s too much “out upon thee”; I pray thee, let me in.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Ay, when fowls have no feathers and fish have no fin.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Well, I’ll break in; go, borrow me a crow.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: A crow without feather; master, mean you so?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: For a fish without a fin, there’s a fowl without a feather.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: If a crow help us in, sirrah, we’ll pluck a crow together.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Go, get thee gone; fetch me an iron crow.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Have patience, sir. O, let it not be so:

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Herein you war against your reputation,

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: And draw within the compass of suspect

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: The unviolated honour of your wife.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Once this,—your long experience of her wisdom,

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Her sober virtue, years, and modesty,

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Plead on her part some cause to you unknown;

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: And doubt not, sir, but she will well excuse

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Why at this time the doors are made against you.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Be rul’d by me; depart in patience,

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: And let us to the Tiger all to dinner,

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: And about evening, come yourself alone

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: To know the reason of this strange restraint.

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: If by strong hand you offer to break in

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Now in the stirring passage of the day,

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: A vulgar comment will be made of it;

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: And that supposed by the common rout

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: Against your yet ungalled estimation

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: That may with foul intrusion enter in,

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: And dwell upon your grave when you are dead;

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: For slander lives upon succession,

lines.speaker: BALTHASAR
lines.text: For ever hous’d where it gets possession.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: You have prevail’d. I will depart in quiet,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And, in despite of mirth, mean to be merry.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I know a wench of excellent discourse,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Pretty and witty; wild, and yet, too, gentle;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: There will we dine. This woman that I mean,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: My wife (but, I protest, without desert)

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Hath oftentimes upbraided me withal;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: To her will we to dinner.—Get you home

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And fetch the chain, by this I know ’tis made.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Bring it, I pray you, to the Porpentine,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: For there’s the house. That chain will I bestow

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: (Be it for nothing but to spite my wife)

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Upon mine hostess there. Good sir, make haste.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Since mine own doors refuse to entertain me,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I’ll knock elsewhere, to see if they’ll disdain me.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: I’ll meet you at that place some hour hence.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Do so; this jest shall cost me some expense.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Luciana with Antipholus of Syracuse.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: And may it be that you have quite forgot

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: A husband’s office? Shall, Antipholus,

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Even in the spring of love, thy love-springs rot?

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Shall love, in building, grow so ruinous?

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: If you did wed my sister for her wealth,

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Then for her wealth’s sake use her with more kindness;

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Or if you like elsewhere, do it by stealth,

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Muffle your false love with some show of blindness.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Let not my sister read it in your eye;

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Be not thy tongue thy own shame’s orator;

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Look sweet, speak fair, become disloyalty;

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Apparel vice like virtue’s harbinger;

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Bear a fair presence though your heart be tainted;

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Teach sin the carriage of a holy saint,

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Be secret-false. What need she be acquainted?

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: What simple thief brags of his own attaint?

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: ’Tis double wrong to truant with your bed

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: And let her read it in thy looks at board.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Shame hath a bastard fame, well managed;

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Ill deeds is doubled with an evil word.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Alas, poor women, make us but believe,

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Being compact of credit, that you love us.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Though others have the arm, show us the sleeve;

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: We in your motion turn, and you may move us.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Then, gentle brother, get you in again;

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Comfort my sister, cheer her, call her wife.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: ’Tis holy sport to be a little vain

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: When the sweet breath of flattery conquers strife.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Sweet mistress, what your name is else, I know not,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Nor by what wonder you do hit on mine;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Less in your knowledge and your grace you show not

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Than our earth’s wonder, more than earth divine.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Teach me, dear creature, how to think and speak;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Lay open to my earthy gross conceit,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Smother’d in errors, feeble, shallow, weak,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: The folded meaning of your words’ deceit.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Against my soul’s pure truth why labour you

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: To make it wander in an unknown field?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Are you a god? would you create me new?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Transform me, then, and to your power I’ll yield.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: But if that I am I, then well I know

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Your weeping sister is no wife of mine,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Nor to her bed no homage do I owe.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Far more, far more, to you do I decline.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: O, train me not, sweet mermaid, with thy note

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: To drown me in thy sister’s flood of tears.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Sing, siren, for thyself, and I will dote;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Spread o’er the silver waves thy golden hairs,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And as a bed I’ll take thee, and there lie,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And, in that glorious supposition think

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: He gains by death that hath such means to die.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Let love, being light, be drowned if she sink!

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: What, are you mad, that you do reason so?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Not mad, but mated; how, I do not know.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: It is a fault that springeth from your eye.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: For gazing on your beams, fair sun, being by.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Gaze where you should, and that will clear your sight.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: As good to wink, sweet love, as look on night.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Why call you me love? Call my sister so.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Thy sister’s sister.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: That’s my sister.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: No,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: It is thyself, mine own self’s better part,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Mine eye’s clear eye, my dear heart’s dearer heart,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: My food, my fortune, and my sweet hope’s aim,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: My sole earth’s heaven, and my heaven’s claim.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: All this my sister is, or else should be.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Call thyself sister, sweet, for I aim thee;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Thee will I love, and with thee lead my life;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Thou hast no husband yet, nor I no wife.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Give me thy hand.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: O, soft, sir, hold you still;

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: I’ll fetch my sister to get her goodwill.
[_Exit Luciana._]
Enter Dromio of Syracuse.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Why, how now, Dromio? where runn’st thou so fast?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Do you know me, sir? Am I Dromio? Am I your man? Am I myself?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Thou art Dromio, thou art my man, thou art thyself.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I am an ass, I am a woman’s man, and besides myself.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What woman’s man? and how besides thyself?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Marry, sir, besides myself, I am due to a woman, one that claims me,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: one that haunts me, one that will have me.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What claim lays she to thee?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Marry, sir, such claim as you would lay to your horse, and she would

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: have me as a beast; not that I being a beast she would have me, but

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: that she being a very beastly creature lays claim to me.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What is she?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: A very reverent body; ay, such a one as a man may not speak of without

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: he say “sir-reverence”. I have but lean luck in the match, and yet is

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: she a wondrous fat marriage.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: How dost thou mean a “fat marriage”?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Marry, sir, she’s the kitchen wench, and all grease, and I know not

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: what use to put her to but to make a lamp of her and run from her by

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: her own light. I warrant her rags and the tallow in them will burn a

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Poland winter. If she lives till doomsday, she’ll burn a week longer

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: than the whole world.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What complexion is she of?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Swart like my shoe, but her face nothing like so clean kept. For why?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: she sweats, a man may go overshoes in the grime of it.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: That’s a fault that water will mend.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: No, sir, ’tis in grain; Noah’s flood could not do it.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What’s her name?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Nell, sir; but her name and three quarters, that’s an ell and three

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: quarters, will not measure her from hip to hip.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Then she bears some breadth?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: No longer from head to foot than from hip to hip. She is spherical,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: like a globe. I could find out countries in her.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: In what part of her body stands Ireland?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Marry, sir, in her buttocks; I found it out by the bogs.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Where Scotland?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I found it by the barrenness, hard in the palm of the hand.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Where France?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: In her forehead; armed and reverted, making war against her hair.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Where England?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I looked for the chalky cliffs, but I could find no whiteness in them.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: But I guess it stood in her chin, by the salt rheum that ran between

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: France and it.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Where Spain?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Faith, I saw it not; but I felt it hot in her breath.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Where America, the Indies?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: O, sir, upon her nose, all o’er-embellished with rubies, carbuncles,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: sapphires, declining their rich aspect to the hot breath of Spain, who

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: sent whole armadoes of carracks to be ballast at her nose.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Where stood Belgia, the Netherlands?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: O, sir, I did not look so low. To conclude: this drudge or diviner laid

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: claim to me, called me Dromio, swore I was assured to her, told me what

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: privy marks I had about me, as the mark of my shoulder, the mole in my

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: neck, the great wart on my left arm, that I, amazed, ran from her as a

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: witch. And, I think, if my breast had not been made of faith, and my

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: heart of steel, she had transformed me to a curtal dog, and made me

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: turn i’ the wheel.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Go, hie thee presently, post to the road;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And if the wind blow any way from shore,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I will not harbour in this town tonight.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: If any bark put forth, come to the mart,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Where I will walk till thou return to me.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: If everyone knows us, and we know none,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: ’Tis time, I think, to trudge, pack and be gone.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: As from a bear a man would run for life,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: So fly I from her that would be my wife.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: There’s none but witches do inhabit here,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And therefore ’tis high time that I were hence.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: She that doth call me husband, even my soul

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Doth for a wife abhor. But her fair sister,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Possess’d with such a gentle sovereign grace,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Of such enchanting presence and discourse,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Hath almost made me traitor to myself.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: But lest myself be guilty to self-wrong,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I’ll stop mine ears against the mermaid’s song.
Enter Angelo with the chain.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Master Antipholus.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Ay, that’s my name.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: I know it well, sir. Lo, here is the chain;

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: I thought to have ta’en you at the Porpentine,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: The chain unfinish’d made me stay thus long.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What is your will that I shall do with this?

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: What please yourself, sir; I have made it for you.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Made it for me, sir! I bespoke it not.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Not once, nor twice, but twenty times you have.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Go home with it, and please your wife withal,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: And soon at supper-time I’ll visit you,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: And then receive my money for the chain.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I pray you, sir, receive the money now,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: For fear you ne’er see chain nor money more.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: You are a merry man, sir; fare you well.
[_Exit._]

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What I should think of this I cannot tell,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: But this I think, there’s no man is so vain

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: That would refuse so fair an offer’d chain.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I see a man here needs not live by shifts,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: When in the streets he meets such golden gifts.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I’ll to the mart, and there for Dromio stay;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: If any ship put out, then straight away.
[_Exit._]
Enter Merchant, Angelo and an Officer.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: You know since Pentecost the sum is due,

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: And since I have not much importun’d you,

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Nor now I had not, but that I am bound

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: To Persia, and want guilders for my voyage;

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Therefore make present satisfaction,

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Or I’ll attach you by this officer.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Even just the sum that I do owe to you

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Is growing to me by Antipholus,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: And in the instant that I met with you

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: He had of me a chain; at five o’clock

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: I shall receive the money for the same.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Pleaseth you walk with me down to his house,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: I will discharge my bond, and thank you too.
Enter Antipholus of Ephesus and Dromio of Ephesus from the Courtesan’s.

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: That labour may you save. See where he comes.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: While I go to the goldsmith’s house, go thou

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And buy a rope’s end; that will I bestow

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Among my wife and her confederates

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: For locking me out of my doors by day.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But soft, I see the goldsmith; get thee gone;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Buy thou a rope, and bring it home to me.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I buy a thousand pound a year! I buy a rope!
[_Exit Dromio._]

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: A man is well holp up that trusts to you,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I promised your presence and the chain,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But neither chain nor goldsmith came to me.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Belike you thought our love would last too long

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: If it were chain’d together, and therefore came not.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Saving your merry humour, here’s the note

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: How much your chain weighs to the utmost carat,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: The fineness of the gold, and chargeful fashion,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Which doth amount to three odd ducats more

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Than I stand debted to this gentleman.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: I pray you, see him presently discharg’d,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: For he is bound to sea, and stays but for it.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I am not furnished with the present money;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Besides, I have some business in the town.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Good signior, take the stranger to my house,
