lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And with you take the chain, and bid my wife

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Disburse the sum on the receipt thereof;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Perchance I will be there as soon as you.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Then you will bring the chain to her yourself.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: No, bear it with you, lest I come not time enough.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Well, sir, I will. Have you the chain about you?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And if I have not, sir, I hope you have,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Or else you may return without your money.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Nay, come, I pray you, sir, give me the chain;

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Both wind and tide stays for this gentleman,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: And I, to blame, have held him here too long.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Good Lord, you use this dalliance to excuse

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Your breach of promise to the Porpentine.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I should have chid you for not bringing it,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But, like a shrew, you first begin to brawl.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: The hour steals on; I pray you, sir, dispatch.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: You hear how he importunes me. The chain!

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Why, give it to my wife, and fetch your money.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Come, come, you know I gave it you even now.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Either send the chain or send by me some token.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Fie, now you run this humour out of breath.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Come, where’s the chain? I pray you, let me see it.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: My business cannot brook this dalliance.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Good sir, say whe’er you’ll answer me or no;

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: If not, I’ll leave him to the officer.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I answer you? What should I answer you?

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: The money that you owe me for the chain.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I owe you none till I receive the chain.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: You know I gave it you half an hour since.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: You gave me none. You wrong me much to say so.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: You wrong me more, sir, in denying it.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Consider how it stands upon my credit.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Well, officer, arrest him at my suit.

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: I do, and charge you in the duke’s name to obey me.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: This touches me in reputation.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Either consent to pay this sum for me,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Or I attach you by this officer.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Consent to pay thee that I never had?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Arrest me, foolish fellow, if thou dar’st.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Here is thy fee; arrest him, officer.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: I would not spare my brother in this case

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: If he should scorn me so apparently.

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: I do arrest you, sir. You hear the suit.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I do obey thee till I give thee bail.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But, sirrah, you shall buy this sport as dear

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: As all the metal in your shop will answer.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: Sir, sir, I shall have law in Ephesus,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: To your notorious shame, I doubt it not.
Enter Dromio of Syracuse from the bay.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Master, there’s a bark of Epidamnum

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: That stays but till her owner comes aboard,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And then, sir, bears away. Our fraughtage, sir,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I have convey’d aboard, and I have bought

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: The oil, the balsamum, and aqua-vitae.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: The ship is in her trim; the merry wind

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Blows fair from land; they stay for nought at all

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: But for their owner, master, and yourself.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: How now? a madman? Why, thou peevish sheep,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: What ship of Epidamnum stays for me?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: A ship you sent me to, to hire waftage.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Thou drunken slave, I sent thee for a rope,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And told thee to what purpose and what end.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: You sent me for a rope’s end as soon.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: You sent me to the bay, sir, for a bark.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I will debate this matter at more leisure,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And teach your ears to list me with more heed.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: To Adriana, villain, hie thee straight:

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Give her this key, and tell her in the desk

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: That’s cover’d o’er with Turkish tapestry

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: There is a purse of ducats; let her send it.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Tell her I am arrested in the street,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And that shall bail me. Hie thee, slave; be gone.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: On, officer, to prison till it come.
[_Exeunt Merchant, Angelo, Officer and Antipholus of Ephesus._]

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: To Adriana, that is where we din’d,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Where Dowsabel did claim me for her husband.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: She is too big, I hope, for me to compass.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Thither I must, although against my will,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: For servants must their masters’ minds fulfil.
[_Exit._]
Enter Adriana and Luciana.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Ah, Luciana, did he tempt thee so?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Might’st thou perceive austerely in his eye

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: That he did plead in earnest, yea or no?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Look’d he or red or pale, or sad or merrily?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: What observation mad’st thou in this case

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Of his heart’s meteors tilting in his face?

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: First he denied you had in him no right.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: He meant he did me none; the more my spite.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Then swore he that he was a stranger here.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And true he swore, though yet forsworn he were.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Then pleaded I for you.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And what said he?

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: That love I begg’d for you he begg’d of me.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: With what persuasion did he tempt thy love?

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: With words that in an honest suit might move.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: First he did praise my beauty, then my speech.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Did’st speak him fair?

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Have patience, I beseech.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: I cannot, nor I will not hold me still.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: My tongue, though not my heart, shall have his will.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: He is deformed, crooked, old, and sere,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Ill-fac’d, worse bodied, shapeless everywhere;

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Vicious, ungentle, foolish, blunt, unkind,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Stigmatical in making, worse in mind.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Who would be jealous then of such a one?

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: No evil lost is wail’d when it is gone.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Ah, but I think him better than I say,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And yet would herein others’ eyes were worse:

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Far from her nest the lapwing cries away;

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: My heart prays for him, though my tongue do curse.
Enter Dromio of Syracuse.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Here, go; the desk, the purse, sweet now, make haste.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: How hast thou lost thy breath?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: By running fast.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Where is thy master, Dromio? is he well?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: No, he’s in Tartar limbo, worse than hell.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: A devil in an everlasting garment hath him,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: One whose hard heart is button’d up with steel;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: A fiend, a fairy, pitiless and rough;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: A wolf, nay worse, a fellow all in buff;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: A back-friend, a shoulder-clapper, one that countermands

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: The passages of alleys, creeks, and narrow lands;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: A hound that runs counter, and yet draws dryfoot well,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: One that, before the judgement, carries poor souls to hell.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Why, man, what is the matter?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I do not know the matter. He is ’rested on the case.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: What, is he arrested? Tell me at whose suit?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I know not at whose suit he is arrested, well;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: But he’s in a suit of buff which ’rested him, that can I tell.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Will you send him, mistress, redemption, the money in his desk?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Go fetch it, sister. This I wonder at,
[_Exit Luciana._]

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Thus he unknown to me should be in debt.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Tell me, was he arrested on a band?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Not on a band, but on a stronger thing;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: A chain, a chain. Do you not hear it ring?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: What, the chain?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: No, no, the bell, ’tis time that I were gone.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: It was two ere I left him, and now the clock strikes one.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: The hours come back! That did I never hear.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: O yes, if any hour meet a sergeant, ’a turns back for very fear.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: As if time were in debt. How fondly dost thou reason!

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Time is a very bankrupt, and owes more than he’s worth to season.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Nay, he’s a thief too. Have you not heard men say

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: That time comes stealing on by night and day?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: If he be in debt and theft, and a sergeant in the way,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Hath he not reason to turn back an hour in a day?
Enter Luciana.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Go, Dromio, there’s the money, bear it straight,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And bring thy master home immediately.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Come, sister, I am press’d down with conceit;

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Conceit, my comfort and my injury.
[_Exeunt._]
Enter Antipholus of Syracuse.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: There’s not a man I meet but doth salute me

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: As if I were their well-acquainted friend,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And everyone doth call me by my name.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Some tender money to me, some invite me;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Some other give me thanks for kindnesses;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Some offer me commodities to buy.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Even now a tailor call’d me in his shop,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And show’d me silks that he had bought for me,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And therewithal took measure of my body.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Sure, these are but imaginary wiles,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And Lapland sorcerers inhabit here.
Enter Dromio of Syracuse.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Master, here’s the gold you sent me for.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What, have you got the picture of old Adam new apparelled?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What gold is this? What Adam dost thou mean?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Not that Adam that kept the paradise, but that Adam that keeps the

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: prison; he that goes in the calf’s skin that was killed for the

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Prodigal; he that came behind you, sir, like an evil angel, and bid you

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: forsake your liberty.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I understand thee not.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: No? Why, ’tis a plain case: he that went like a bass-viol in a case of

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: leather; the man, sir, that, when gentlemen are tired, gives them a

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: sob, and ’rests them; he, sir, that takes pity on decayed men and gives

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: them suits of durance; he that sets up his rest to do more exploits

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: with his mace than a morris-pike.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: What! thou mean’st an officer?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Ay, sir, the sergeant of the band; he that brings any man to answer it

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: that breaks his band; one that thinks a man always going to bed, and

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: says, “God give you good rest.”

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Well, sir, there rest in your foolery. Is there any ship puts forth

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: tonight? may we be gone?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Why, sir, I brought you word an hour since that the bark _Expedition_

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: put forth tonight, and then were you hindered by the sergeant to tarry

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: for the hoy _Delay_. Here are the angels that you sent for to deliver

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: you.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: The fellow is distract, and so am I,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And here we wander in illusions.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Some blessed power deliver us from hence!
Enter a Courtesan.

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Well met, well met, Master Antipholus.

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: I see, sir, you have found the goldsmith now.

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Is that the chain you promis’d me today?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Satan, avoid! I charge thee, tempt me not.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Master, is this Mistress Satan?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: It is the devil.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Nay, she is worse, she is the devil’s dam; and here she comes in the

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: habit of a light wench, and thereof comes that the wenches say “God

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: damn me”, that’s as much to say, “God make me a light wench.” It is

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: written they appear to men like angels of light. Light is an effect of

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: fire, and fire will burn; ergo, light wenches will burn. Come not near

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: her.

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Your man and you are marvellous merry, sir.

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Will you go with me? We’ll mend our dinner here.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Master, if you do, expect spoon-meat, or bespeak a long spoon.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Why, Dromio?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Marry, he must have a long spoon that must eat with the devil.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Avoid then, fiend! What tell’st thou me of supping?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Thou art, as you are all, a sorceress.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I conjure thee to leave me and be gone.

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Give me the ring of mine you had at dinner,

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Or, for my diamond, the chain you promis’d,

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: And I’ll be gone, sir, and not trouble you.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Some devils ask but the paring of one’s nail,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: A rush, a hair, a drop of blood, a pin,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: A nut, a cherry-stone; but she, more covetous,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Would have a chain.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Master, be wise; and if you give it her,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: The devil will shake her chain and fright us with it.

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: I pray you, sir, my ring, or else the chain;

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: I hope you do not mean to cheat me so.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Avaunt, thou witch! Come, Dromio, let us go.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Fly pride, says the peacock. Mistress, that you know.
[_Exeunt Antipholus of Syracuse and Dromio of Syracuse._]

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Now, out of doubt Antipholus is mad,

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Else would he never so demean himself.

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: A ring he hath of mine worth forty ducats,

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: And for the same he promis’d me a chain;

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Both one and other he denies me now.

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: The reason that I gather he is mad,

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Besides this present instance of his rage,

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Is a mad tale he told today at dinner

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Of his own doors being shut against his entrance.

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Belike his wife, acquainted with his fits,

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: On purpose shut the doors against his way.

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: My way is now to hie home to his house,

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: And tell his wife that, being lunatic,

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: He rush’d into my house and took perforce

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: My ring away. This course I fittest choose,

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: For forty ducats is too much to lose.
[_Exit._]
Enter Antipholus of Ephesus with an Officer.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Fear me not, man, I will not break away:

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I’ll give thee ere I leave thee so much money,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: To warrant thee, as I am ’rested for.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: My wife is in a wayward mood today,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And will not lightly trust the messenger

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: That I should be attach’d in Ephesus;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I tell you ’twill sound harshly in her ears.
Enter Dromio of Ephesus with a rope’s end.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Here comes my man. I think he brings the money.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: How now, sir! have you that I sent you for?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Here’s that, I warrant you, will pay them all.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But where’s the money?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Why, sir, I gave the money for the rope.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Five hundred ducats, villain, for a rope?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I’ll serve you, sir, five hundred at the rate.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: To what end did I bid thee hie thee home?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: To a rope’s end, sir; and to that end am I return’d.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And to that end, sir, I will welcome you.
[_Beating him._]

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: Good sir, be patient.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Nay, ’tis for me to be patient. I am in adversity.

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: Good now, hold thy tongue.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Nay, rather persuade him to hold his hands.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Thou whoreson, senseless villain.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I would I were senseless, sir, that I might not feel your blows.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Thou art sensible in nothing but blows, and so is an ass.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I am an ass indeed; you may prove it by my long ears. I have served him

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: from the hour of my nativity to this instant, and have nothing at his

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: hands for my service but blows. When I am cold, he heats me with

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: beating; when I am warm he cools me with beating. I am waked with it

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: when I sleep, raised with it when I sit, driven out of doors with it

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: when I go from home, welcomed home with it when I return. Nay, I bear

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: it on my shoulders as a beggar wont her brat; and I think when he hath

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: lamed me, I shall beg with it from door to door.
Enter Adriana, Luciana, Courtesan and a Schoolmaster called Pinch.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Come, go along, my wife is coming yonder.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Mistress, _respice finem_, respect your end, or rather, the prophesy

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: like the parrot, “Beware the rope’s end.”

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Wilt thou still talk?
[_Beats him._]

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: How say you now? Is not your husband mad?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: His incivility confirms no less.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Good Doctor Pinch, you are a conjurer;

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Establish him in his true sense again,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And I will please you what you will demand.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Alas, how fiery and how sharp he looks!

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Mark how he trembles in his ecstasy.

lines.speaker: PINCH
lines.text: Give me your hand, and let me feel your pulse.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: There is my hand, and let it feel your ear.

lines.speaker: PINCH
lines.text: I charge thee, Satan, hous’d within this man,

lines.speaker: PINCH
lines.text: To yield possession to my holy prayers,

lines.speaker: PINCH
lines.text: And to thy state of darkness hie thee straight.

lines.speaker: PINCH
lines.text: I conjure thee by all the saints in heaven.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Peace, doting wizard, peace; I am not mad.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: O, that thou wert not, poor distressed soul!

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: You minion, you, are these your customers?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Did this companion with the saffron face

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Revel and feast it at my house today,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Whilst upon me the guilty doors were shut,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And I denied to enter in my house?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: O husband, God doth know you din’d at home,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Where would you had remain’d until this time,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Free from these slanders and this open shame.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Din’d at home? Thou villain, what sayest thou?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Sir, sooth to say, you did not dine at home.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Were not my doors lock’d up and I shut out?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Perdy, your doors were lock’d, and you shut out.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And did not she herself revile me there?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Sans fable, she herself revil’d you there.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Did not her kitchen-maid rail, taunt, and scorn me?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Certes, she did, the kitchen-vestal scorn’d you.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And did not I in rage depart from thence?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: In verity, you did; my bones bear witness,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: That since have felt the vigour of his rage.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Is’t good to soothe him in these contraries?

lines.speaker: PINCH
lines.text: It is no shame; the fellow finds his vein,

lines.speaker: PINCH
lines.text: And yielding to him, humours well his frenzy.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Thou hast suborn’d the goldsmith to arrest me.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Alas! I sent you money to redeem you

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: By Dromio here, who came in haste for it.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Money by me? Heart and goodwill you might,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But surely, master, not a rag of money.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Went’st not thou to her for a purse of ducats?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: He came to me, and I deliver’d it.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: And I am witness with her that she did.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: God and the rope-maker bear me witness

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: That I was sent for nothing but a rope.

lines.speaker: PINCH
lines.text: Mistress, both man and master is possess’d,

lines.speaker: PINCH
lines.text: I know it by their pale and deadly looks.

lines.speaker: PINCH
lines.text: They must be bound and laid in some dark room.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Say, wherefore didst thou lock me forth today,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And why dost thou deny the bag of gold?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: I did not, gentle husband, lock thee forth.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And gentle master, I receiv’d no gold;

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But I confess, sir, that we were lock’d out.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Dissembling villain, thou speak’st false in both.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Dissembling harlot, thou art false in all,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And art confederate with a damned pack

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: To make a loathsome abject scorn of me.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But with these nails I’ll pluck out these false eyes

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: That would behold in me this shameful sport.
[_Enter three or four, and offer to bind him. He strives. _]

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: O, bind him, bind him; let him not come near me.

lines.speaker: PINCH
lines.text: More company; the fiend is strong within him.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: Ay me, poor man, how pale and wan he looks!

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: What, will you murder me? Thou jailer, thou,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I am thy prisoner. Wilt thou suffer them

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: To make a rescue?

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: Masters, let him go.

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: He is my prisoner, and you shall not have him.

lines.speaker: PINCH
lines.text: Go, bind this man, for he is frantic too.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: What wilt thou do, thou peevish officer?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Hast thou delight to see a wretched man

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Do outrage and displeasure to himself?

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: He is my prisoner. If I let him go,

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: The debt he owes will be requir’d of me.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: I will discharge thee ere I go from thee;

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Bear me forthwith unto his creditor,

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And knowing how the debt grows, I will pay it.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Good master doctor, see him safe convey’d

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Home to my house. O most unhappy day!

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: O most unhappy strumpet!

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Master, I am here enter’d in bond for you.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Out on thee, villain! wherefore dost thou mad me?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Will you be bound for nothing? Be mad, good master; cry, “the devil”.

lines.speaker: LUCIANA
lines.text: God help, poor souls, how idly do they talk!

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Go bear him hence. Sister, go you with me.
[_Exeunt Pinch and Assistants, with Antipholus of Ephesus and Dromio of Ephesus._]

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Say now, whose suit is he arrested at?

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: One Angelo, a goldsmith; do you know him?

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: I know the man. What is the sum he owes?

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: Two hundred ducats.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Say, how grows it due?

lines.speaker: OFFICER
lines.text: Due for a chain your husband had of him.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: He did bespeak a chain for me, but had it not.

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: When as your husband, all in rage, today

lines.speaker: COURTESAN

lines.text: For these deep shames and great indignities.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: My lord, in truth, thus far I witness with him,

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: That he din’d not at home, but was lock’d out.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: But had he such a chain of thee, or no?

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: He had, my lord, and when he ran in here

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: These people saw the chain about his neck.

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Besides, I will be sworn these ears of mine

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: Heard you confess you had the chain of him,

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: After you first forswore it on the mart,

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: And thereupon I drew my sword on you;

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: And then you fled into this abbey here,

lines.speaker: MERCHANT
lines.text: From whence I think you are come by miracle.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I never came within these abbey walls,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Nor ever didst thou draw thy sword on me.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I never saw the chain, so help me heaven;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And this is false you burden me withal.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Why, what an intricate impeach is this!

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I think you all have drunk of Circe’s cup.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: If here you hous’d him, here he would have been.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: If he were mad, he would not plead so coldly.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: You say he din’d at home, the goldsmith here

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Denies that saying. Sirrah, what say you?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Sir, he dined with her there, at the Porpentine.

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: He did, and from my finger snatch’d that ring.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: ’Tis true, my liege, this ring I had of her.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Saw’st thou him enter at the abbey here?

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: As sure, my liege, as I do see your grace.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Why, this is strange. Go call the abbess hither.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I think you are all mated, or stark mad.
[_Exit one to the Abbess._]

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Most mighty Duke, vouchsafe me speak a word;

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Haply I see a friend will save my life

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And pay the sum that may deliver me.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Speak freely, Syracusian, what thou wilt.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Is not your name, sir, call’d Antipholus?

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And is not that your bondman Dromio?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Within this hour I was his bondman, sir,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: But he, I thank him, gnaw’d in two my cords.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Now am I Dromio, and his man, unbound.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: I am sure you both of you remember me.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Ourselves we do remember, sir, by you.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: For lately we were bound as you are now.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: You are not Pinch’s patient, are you, sir?

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Why look you strange on me? you know me well.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I never saw you in my life till now.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: O! grief hath chang’d me since you saw me last,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And careful hours with time’s deformed hand,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Have written strange defeatures in my face.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: But tell me yet, dost thou not know my voice?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Neither.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Dromio, nor thou?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: No, trust me, sir, nor I.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: I am sure thou dost.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Ay, sir, but I am sure I do not, and whatsoever a man denies, you are

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: now bound to believe him.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Not know my voice! O time’s extremity,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Hast thou so crack’d and splitted my poor tongue

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: In seven short years that here my only son

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Knows not my feeble key of untun’d cares?

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Though now this grained face of mine be hid

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: In sap-consuming winter’s drizzled snow,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: And all the conduits of my blood froze up,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Yet hath my night of life some memory,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: My wasting lamps some fading glimmer left,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: My dull deaf ears a little use to hear.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: All these old witnesses, I cannot err,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Tell me thou art my son Antipholus.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I never saw my father in my life.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: But seven years since, in Syracusa, boy,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Thou know’st we parted; but perhaps, my son,

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: Thou sham’st to acknowledge me in misery.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: The duke and all that know me in the city,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Can witness with me that it is not so.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I ne’er saw Syracusa in my life.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I tell thee, Syracusian, twenty years

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Have I been patron to Antipholus,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: During which time he ne’er saw Syracusa.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: I see thy age and dangers make thee dote.
Enter the Abbess with Antipholus of Syracuse and Dromio of Syracuse.

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: Most mighty duke, behold a man much wrong’d.
[_All gather to see them._]

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: I see two husbands, or mine eyes deceive me.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: One of these men is _genius_ to the other;

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And so of these, which is the natural man,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And which the spirit? Who deciphers them?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I, sir, am Dromio, command him away.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I, sir, am Dromio, pray let me stay.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Egeon, art thou not? or else his ghost?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: O, my old master, who hath bound him here?

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: Whoever bound him, I will loose his bonds,

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: And gain a husband by his liberty.

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: Speak, old Egeon, if thou be’st the man

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: That hadst a wife once called Emilia,

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: That bore thee at a burden two fair sons.

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: O, if thou be’st the same Egeon, speak,

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: And speak unto the same Emilia!

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Why, here begins his morning story right:

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: These two Antipholus’, these two so like,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: And these two Dromios, one in semblance,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Besides her urging of her wreck at sea.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: These are the parents to these children,

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Which accidentally are met together.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: If I dream not, thou art Emilia.

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: If thou art she, tell me where is that son

lines.speaker: EGEON
lines.text: That floated with thee on the fatal raft?

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: By men of Epidamnum, he and I

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: And the twin Dromio, all were taken up;

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: But, by and by, rude fishermen of Corinth

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: By force took Dromio and my son from them,

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: And me they left with those of Epidamnum.

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: What then became of them I cannot tell;

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: I to this fortune that you see me in.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Antipholus, thou cam’st from Corinth first?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: No, sir, not I, I came from Syracuse.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: Stay, stand apart, I know not which is which.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I came from Corinth, my most gracious lord.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And I with him.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Brought to this town by that most famous warrior,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Duke Menaphon, your most renowned uncle.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: Which of you two did dine with me today?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I, gentle mistress.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: And are not you my husband?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: No, I say nay to that.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And so do I, yet did she call me so;

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And this fair gentlewoman, her sister here,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Did call me brother. What I told you then,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I hope I shall have leisure to make good,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: If this be not a dream I see and hear.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: That is the chain, sir, which you had of me.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I think it be, sir. I deny it not.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And you, sir, for this chain arrested me.

lines.speaker: ANGELO
lines.text: I think I did, sir. I deny it not.

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: I sent you money, sir, to be your bail

lines.speaker: ADRIANA
lines.text: By Dromio, but I think he brought it not.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: No, none by me.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: This purse of ducats I receiv’d from you,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And Dromio my man did bring them me.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: I see we still did meet each other’s man,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And I was ta’en for him, and he for me,

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: And thereupon these errors are arose.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: These ducats pawn I for my father here.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: It shall not need, thy father hath his life.

lines.speaker: COURTESAN
lines.text: Sir, I must have that diamond from you.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: There, take it, and much thanks for my good cheer.

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: Renowned duke, vouchsafe to take the pains

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: To go with us into the abbey here,

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: And hear at large discoursed all our fortunes;

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: And all that are assembled in this place,

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: That by this sympathised one day’s error

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: Have suffer’d wrong, go, keep us company,

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: And we shall make full satisfaction.

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: Thirty-three years have I but gone in travail

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: Of you, my sons, and till this present hour

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: My heavy burden ne’er delivered.

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: The duke, my husband, and my children both,

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: And you, the calendars of their nativity,

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: Go to a gossips’ feast, and go with me.

lines.speaker: ABBESS
lines.text: After so long grief, such nativity.

lines.speaker: DUKE
lines.text: With all my heart, I’ll gossip at this feast.
[_Exeunt except the two Dromios and two Brothers._]

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Master, shall I fetch your stuff from shipboard?

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Dromio, what stuff of mine hast thou embark’d?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Your goods that lay at host, sir, in the Centaur.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: He speaks to me; I am your master, Dromio.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Come, go with us. We’ll look to that anon.

lines.speaker: ANTIPHOLUS OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Embrace thy brother there, rejoice with him.
[_Exeunt Antipholus of Syracuse and Antipholus of Ephesus._]

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: There is a fat friend at your master’s house,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: That kitchen’d me for you today at dinner.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: She now shall be my sister, not my wife.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Methinks you are my glass, and not my brother.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: I see by you I am a sweet-faced youth.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Will you walk in to see their gossiping?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: Not I, sir, you are my elder.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: That’s a question, how shall we try it?

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF SYRACUSE
lines.text: We’ll draw cuts for the senior. Till then, lead thou first.

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: Nay, then, thus:

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: We came into the world like brother and brother,

lines.speaker: DROMIO OF EPHESUS
lines.text: And now let’s go hand in hand, not one before another.
[_Exeunt._]
